verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              अनागतविधाता च प्रत्युत्पन्नमतिश्च यः । द्वावेव सुखमेधेते दीर्घसूत्री विनश्यति ॥१॥
verses.english: You should, O grandfather, describe to me what is freed from duty and its reverse, what is freed from every doubt, what is above birth and death, as also virtue and sin, what is auspiciousness, what is eternal fearlessness, what is Eternal and Indestructible, and Immutable, what is always Pure, and what is ever free from exertion.

verses.sanskrit: अत्रैव चेदमव्यग्रं शृणुष्वाख्यानमुत्तमम् । दीर्घं सूत्रमुपाश्रित्य कार्याकार्यविनिश्चये ॥२॥
verses.english: Bhishma said O Bharata, referring to this matter I shall recite to you the old discourse between Yajnavalkya and Janaka. Once on a time the famous king Daivarati of Janaka's race, truthfully understanding the meaning of all questions, put this question to Yajnavalkya, that foremost of Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: नातिगाधे जलाधारे सुहृदः कुशलास्त्रयः । प्रभूतमत्स्ये कौन्तेय बभूवुः सहचारिणः ॥३॥
verses.english: Janaka said ( regenerate Rishi, how many kinds of senses are there? How many kinds also are there of Nature? What is the Unmanifest and highest Brahma? What is higher than Brahmana? What is Birth and what Death? What are the limits of Age? You should, O foremost of Brahmanas, describe all these subjects to me who seek your favour.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रैको दीर्घकालज्ञ उत्पन्नप्रतिभोऽपरः । दीर्घसूत्रश्च तत्रैकस्त्रयाणां सहचारिणाम् ॥४॥
verses.english: I am ignorant while you are an Ocean of knowledge. Hence, I ask you. Verily, I wish to hear you describe all these subject.

verses.sanskrit: कदाचित् तं जलस्थायं मत्स्यबन्धाः समन्ततः । निस्त्रावयामासुरथो निम्नेषु विविधैर्मुखैः ॥५॥
verses.english: Hear, O king, what I say in answer to these questions of yours. I shall give you the high knowledge which Yogins prize, and especially that which is possessed by the Sankhyas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रक्षीयमाणं तं दृष्ट्वा जलस्थायं भयागमे । अब्रवीद्दीर्घदर्शी तु तावुभौ सुहृदौ तदा ॥६॥
verses.english: Nothing is unknown to you. Still you ask me. One, however, who is questioned, should answer. This is the eternal practice.

verses.sanskrit: इयमापत्समुत्पन्ना सर्वेषां सलिलौकसाम् । शीघ्रमन्यत्र गच्छामः पन्था यावन्न दुष्यति ॥७॥
verses.english: Eight principles have been called by the name of Nature, while sixteen have been called changes. Of Manifest, there are seven. These are of views of those persons who are conversant with the spiritual science.

verses.sanskrit: अनागतमनर्थं हि सुनयैर्यः प्रबाधयेत् । स न संशयमाप्नोति रोचतां भो व्रजामहे ॥८॥
verses.english: The Unmanifest, Greatness, Consciousness and the five subtile elements of Earth, Wind, Ether, water, and Light, these eight are known by the name of Nature. Listen now to the enumeration of those called changes. They are the ear, the skin, the eye, the tongue' and the nose; and sound, touch, form, taste, and scent, as also speech, the two arins, the two feet, the lower duct (within the body), and the organ of pleasure.

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घसूत्रस्तु यस्तत्र सोऽब्रवीत्सम्यगुच्यते । न त कार्या त्वरा तावदिति मे निश्चिता मतिः ॥९॥
verses.english: The ten commencing with sound, and originating from the five great principles, are called Vishesha. The five senses of knowledge are called Savishesha, O king of Mithila.

verses.sanskrit: अथ सम्प्रतिपत्तिज्ञः प्राब्रवीद्दीर्घदर्शिनम् । प्राप्ते काले न मे किञ्चिन्यायतः परिहास्यते ॥१०॥
verses.english: Persons conversant with the spiritual science consider the Mind as the sixteenth. This is agreeable to your own views as also to those of other learned men well acquainted with the truths about principles.

verses.sanskrit: एवं श्रुत्वा निराक्रम्य दीर्घदर्शी महामतिः । जगाम स्रोतसा तेन गम्भीरं सलिलाशयम् ॥११॥
verses.english: From the Unmanifest, O king, originates the Greatness. The learned say this to be the first creation relating to Nature.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रसृततोयं तं प्रसमीक्ष्य जलाशयम् । बबन्धुर्विविधैर्योगैर्मत्स्यान्मत्स्योपजीविनः ॥१२॥
verses.english: From Greatness, O king of men, originates Consciousness. This has been designated the second creation having the Understanding for its essence.

verses.sanskrit: विलोड्यमाने तस्मिंस्तु स्रुततोये जलाशये । अगच्छद्बन्धनं तत्र दीर्घसूत्रः सहापरैः ॥१३॥
verses.english: From Consciousness has originated the Mind which is the essence of sound and the others that are the qualities of ether and the rest. This is the third creation, relating to Consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: उद्याने क्रियमाणे तु मत्स्यानां तत्र रज्जुभिः । प्रविश्यान्तरमेतेषां स्थितः सम्प्रतिपत्तिमान् ॥१४॥
verses.english: From Mind have originated the great elements, O king! This is the fourth creation called mental.

verses.sanskrit: गृह्यमेव तदुद्यानं गृहीत्वा तं तथैव सः । सर्वानेव च तांस्तत्र ते विदुर्ग्रथितानिति ॥१५॥
ततः प्रक्षाल्यमानेषु मत्स्येषु विपुले जले । मुक्त्वा रज्जुं प्रमुक्तोऽसौ शीघ्रं सम्प्रतिपत्तिमान् ॥१६॥
verses.english: Persons conversant with the principal elements hold that Sound and Touch and Form and Taste and Scent are the fifth creation, relating to the Great elements.

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घसूत्रस्तु मन्दात्मा हीनबुद्धिरचेतनः । मरणं प्राप्तवान् मूढो यथैवोपहतेन्द्रियः ॥१७॥
verses.english: The creation of the Ear, the Skin, the Eye, the Tongue, and the Scent, forms the sixth and is considered as having for its essence multiplicity of thought.

verses.sanskrit: एवं प्राप्ततमं कालं यो मोहान्नावबुद्ध्यते । स विनश्यति वै क्षिप्रं दीर्घसूत्रो यथा झषः ॥१८॥
verses.english: The senses that come after the Ear and the others then originate, O king. This is called seventh creation and relates to the senses of knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: आदौ न कुरुते श्रेयः कुशलोऽस्मीति यः पुमान् । स संशयमवाप्नोति यथा सम्प्रतिपत्तिमान् ॥१९॥
verses.english: Then, O king, come the vital air that rises upwards and those that go downwards. This is the eighth creation and called Arjjva (straight).

verses.sanskrit: अनागतविधाता च प्रत्युत्पन्नमतिश्च यः । द्वावेव सुखमेधेते दीर्घसूत्रो विनश्यति ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then come those vital airs which move transversely in the lower parts of the body and also that called Apana passing downwards. This, the ninth creation, is also called Arjjava, O king.

verses.sanskrit: काष्ठाः कला मुहूर्ताश्च दिवा रात्रिस्तथा लवाः । मासाः पक्षाः षड् ऋतवः कल्पः संवत्सरास्तथा ॥२१॥
verses.english: These nine kinds of creation, and these principles, O king, which are twenty-four in number, are described to you according to what has been laid down in the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: पृथिवी देश इत्युक्तः कालः स च न दृश्यते । अभिप्रेतार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं ध्यायते यच्च तत्तथा ॥२२॥
verses.english: After this, O king, listen to me as I tell you the durations of time as said by the learned regarding these principles or attributes.

verses.sanskrit: एतौ धर्मार्थशास्त्रेषु मोक्षशास्त्रेषु चर्षिभिः । प्रधानाविति निर्दिष्टौ कामे चाभिमतौ नृणाम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Therefore, the person of forethought and the person of presence of mind, have been described by the Rishis, to be the foremost of men in all works on virtue, profit and emancipation.

verses.sanskrit: परीक्ष्यकारी युक्तश्च स सम्यगुपपादयेत् । देशकालावभिप्रेतौ ताभ्यां फलमवाप्नुयात् ॥२४॥
verses.english: One, however, who does everything after reflection and scrutiny, one, who takes the advantage of proper means for the achievement of his objects, always succeeds in achieving much. Those, again, who work with proper attention to time and place, succeed in acquiring fruits better than the mere man of foresight and the man of presence of mind.'
